### R33. Imaginary-gauge intertwining and zero-energy identities for the integer Hatano-Nelson chain

- **Statement.** For integers r, l and every N: the open Hatano-Nelson matrix with hoppings r², l² satisfies H·D = D·S entrywise for the gauge diagonal D and symmetric path S. Its characteristic recurrence satisfies P_2m(0) = (−1)^m (rl)^(2m), P_(2m+1)(0) = 0. The two-corner determinant formula holds for N = 3, 4. If 0 < l < r then l^(2m) < r^(2m).
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Monodromia.Palomar.t1_hatano_nelson_gbz`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L19), [`Monodromia.HatanoNelsonGBZ.hn_obc_matrix_similarity`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/HatanoNelsonGBZ.lean#L38), [`Monodromia.HatanoNelsonGBZ.hn_dual_corner_det4`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/HatanoNelsonGBZ.lean#L109), [`Monodromia.HatanoNelsonGBZ.hn_exponential_corner_catastrophe`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/HatanoNelsonGBZ.lean#L117); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Link from the corner formula to spectra of general N rests on a determinant identity proven only for N = 3, 4.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** The 'exponential corner catastrophe' conjunct is a power identity; no perturbed spectrum or eigenvalue is formalized.
- **Limit.** The dual-corner determinant formula is proven for N = 3 and 4 only.
- **Limit.** Integer parameters only; no floating-point or numerical-analysis statement is proven.
- **Limit.** The imaginary-gauge picture is classical (Hatano-Nelson); boundary fragility of the skin effect is in Guo et al., PRL 127, 116801 (2021).
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [monodromia](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-014` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-014_monodromia/Donahue_2026_Monodromia.pdf)

<a id="r34"></a>
### R34. Eigenvector identities for a corner-perturbed Jordan block of any order

- **Statement.** For n ≥ 1 and integers λ₀, w: Nⁿ = 0 for the shift matrix with (N^(n−1))_(0,n−1) = 1; eigenvectors of J_n(λ₀) vanish beyond index 0; (w^j), (w^(n−1−j)) are right and left eigenvectors of J_n + wⁿe_(n−1)e₀ᵀ for λ₀ + w; ⟨L,R⟩² = n²w^(2n−2); |L|²|R|² = S_n(w²)²; for integer q > 0, n ≥ 2: S_n(q)² > 1, S_n(q) < S_(n+1)(q).
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Monodromia.Palomar.t2_exceptional_point_petermann`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L21), [`Monodromia.ExceptionalPoints.ep_puiseux_right_eigenvector`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/ExceptionalPoints.lean#L156), [`Monodromia.ExceptionalPoints.ep_petermann_exact_cancellation_bridge`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/ExceptionalPoints.lean#L354), [`Monodromia.ExceptionalPoints.ep_petermann_snr_strictly_below_one`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/ExceptionalPoints.lean#L343); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. The quotient SNR_Pet² = 1/S_n(q)² and any Petermann or sensitivity quantity are formed on paper, not in Lean.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: overlapping earlier or parallel work found (see Limits).
- **Limit.** Covers one model: a single Jordan block with the corner perturbation wⁿ, w an integer.
- **Limit.** No signal-to-noise ratio, Petermann factor or eigenvalue derivative is defined in Lean.
- **Limit.** Order-n Petermann-factor scaling is known at leading order (Wiersig, Phys. Rev. Research 5, 033042 (2023)); only the exact finite-q factor for this model may be new, and that was not searched.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [monodromia](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-014` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-014_monodromia/Donahue_2026_Monodromia.pdf)

<a id="r35"></a>
### R35. Lucas trace and determinant identities for powers of [[2,1],[1,1]]

- **Statement.** For M = [[2,1],[1,1]] and p ≥ 1: tr(Mᵖ) = L_2p and −det(I − Mᵖ) = L_2p − 2; L_2p − 2 ≠ L_2q − 2 for p ≠ q; L_4m − 2 is not the square of any integer for m ≥ 1. Two fixed reduced Burau matrices over Laurent polynomials satisfy the braid relation.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Monodromia.Palomar.t3b_burau_lucas_jones_and_fox_trapezoidal`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L25), [`Monodromia.SpectralKnots.burau_yang_baxter`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/SpectralKnots.lean#L73), [`Monodromia.SpectralKnots.gerono_knot_determinant_lucas`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/SpectralKnots.lean#L132), [`Monodromia.SpectralKnots.gerono_even_not_fox_milnor_square`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/SpectralKnots.lean#L313); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. M is not proven equal to the Burau image of σ₁σ₂⁻¹ at t = −1 in Lean; knot determinants and Fox-Milnor are cited, not formalized.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** Non-sliceness is not a Lean statement; via Fox-Milnor it applies only to even p not divisible by 3, since for 3 | p the closure of (σ₁σ₂⁻¹)ᵖ is a 3-component link.
- **Limit.** The values L_2p − 2 are known determinants of Turk's head links THK(3,p) (OEIS A004146, comment of 2014).
- **Limit.** The braid family is the known lemniscate-of-Gerono family (Bode, Dennis, Foster, King, arXiv:1611.02563, after Perron).
- **Limit.** This is not progress on the slice-ribbon conjecture (GEOM-038).
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [monodromia](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-014` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-014_monodromia/Donahue_2026_Monodromia.pdf)

<a id="r36"></a>
### R36. Finite TL₃ bracket evaluations and trapezoidality of two coefficient lists

- **Statement.** In a hand-coded 5-dimensional Temperley-Lieb model TL₃: the closure brackets of (s₁s₂⁻¹)ᵖ for p = 1, 2, 3, 4 equal explicit Laurent lists; the first is 1, the others differ from it and are palindromic; the bracket of s₁³s₂ differs from that of its mirror. The list of 2m+1 ones and the list [p, 2p+1, p] (p ≥ 1) satisfy the trapezoidal predicate.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Monodromia.SpectralKnots.tl3_gerono_jones_polynomials`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/SpectralKnots.lean#L340), [`Monodromia.SpectralKnots.tl3_trefoil_chiral_separation`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/SpectralKnots.lean#L354), [`Monodromia.SpectralKnots.fox_trapezoidal_torus_2_odd`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/SpectralKnots.lean#L360), [`Monodromia.SpectralKnots.fox_trapezoidal_all_twist_knots`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/SpectralKnots.lean#L375); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Identification of the lists with Jones or Alexander polynomials of named knots is not formalized.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** The lists are typed in by hand; no knot, Alexander polynomial or Jones polynomial is defined in Lean.
- **Limit.** Torus knots T(2,2m+1) and twist knots are two-bridge, a class for which Fox's trapezoidal conjecture is already proved (atlas GEOM-046 row; Hartley 1979 per the literature report).
- **Limit.** [p, 2p+1, p] covers one parity of twist knots only (standard formula, not source-checked).
- **Limit.** 4₁, the Borromean rings and 8₁₈ are table knots/links; this has no bearing on the Jones unknot question (GEOM-039).
- **Limit.** The paper names the trefoil braid σ₁²σ₂ while Lean uses s₁³s₂.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [monodromia](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-014` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-014_monodromia/Donahue_2026_Monodromia.pdf)

<a id="r37"></a>
### R37. Discriminant sign and exceptional-point nilpotency for a non-reciprocal 2×2 integer system

- **Statement.** For integers r_A, r_B, J_AB, J_BA: J_AB·J_BA ≥ 0 implies (r_A − r_B)² + 4J_AB·J_BA ≥ 0; if that discriminant is 0, S = [[r_A−r_B, 2J_AB],[2J_BA, r_B−r_A]] satisfies S² = 0, and S ≠ 0 unless J_AB = J_BA = 0. At ψ_A = isR, ψ_B = R, r = R², s² = 1, the cubic field is tangential with moment −sJR².
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Monodromia.Palomar.t4_non_reciprocal_cep_and_chiral_matter`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L27), [`Monodromia.NonReciprocalCEP.nr_cep_jordan_defective`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/NonReciprocalCEP.lean#L29), [`Monodromia.NonReciprocalCEP.nr_chiral_quadrature_time_crystal`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/NonReciprocalCEP.lean#L52); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Pointwise algebraic identities only; no differential equation, orbit or stability statement.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** No time crystal, limit cycle or attraction is formalized.
- **Limit.** The 'non-variational curl' conjunct is J_AB ≠ J_BA ⇒ J_AB − J_BA ≠ 0, with the curl defined as subtraction.
- **Limit.** The discriminant facts are textbook properties of real 2×2 matrices.
- **Limit.** Atlas CM-043 asks about many-body time crystals and excludes limit-cycle synchronization; this result does not bear on it.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [monodromia](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-014` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-014_monodromia/Donahue_2026_Monodromia.pdf)

<a id="r38"></a>
### R38. Intertwining metric and its positivity for the PT-symmetric dimer over the Gaussian integers

- **Statement.** For integers g, k with H = [[ig, k],[k, −ig]] and η = [[k, −ig],[ig, k]] over ℤ[i]: ηH = H†η; if 0 < k and g² < k², then Re(v†ηv) > 0 for every nonzero Gaussian-integer vector v; at g = k ≠ 0 the vector (1, −i) has η-norm 0.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`Monodromia.Palomar.t5_pt_symmetry_and_pseudo_hermitian_metric`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/PalomarSolution.lean#L29), [`Monodromia.PTSymmetryMetric.pt_metric_intertwining`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/PTSymmetryMetric.lean#L22), [`Monodromia.PTSymmetryMetric.pt_unbroken_metric_pos_def`](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia/blob/153792bdaee2b01f9a56afbcb60af7d2957d5669/lean/MonodromiaProofs/PTSymmetryMetric.lean#L43); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Reality of eigenvalues and impossibility of a positive metric in the broken phase are paper-level; their Lean conjuncts are scalar arithmetic.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** Positivity is shown over Gaussian-integer vectors and integer parameters, not complex vectors or real parameters.
- **Limit.** The T5 conjuncts named 'universal pseudo-Hermitian reality' and 'broken-PT metric impossibility' do not quantify over metrics; the latter holds with the PT hypotheses removed.
- **Limit.** The dimer and its metric are the standard example (Bender-Boettcher 1998; Mostafazadeh 2002).
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [monodromia](https://github.com/0thernes/monodromia) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-014` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-014_monodromia/Donahue_2026_Monodromia.pdf)

<a id="r39"></a>
### R39. Kernel-checked lower bounds for C₂₇ and C₃₁ that are weaker than published values

- **Statement.** C₂₇^⊠2048 and C₃₁^⊠2048 contain independent sets of sizes M₂₇ and M₃₁ with 13319390984674515^2048 ≤ M₂₇·10^(15·2048) and 15308776193986504^2048 ≤ M₃₁·10^(15·2048). Consequently Θ(C₂₇) ≥ 13.319390984674515 and Θ(C₃₁) ≥ 15.308776193986504. Both are smaller than 31522^(1/4) ≈ 13.3246 and 54934^(1/4) ≈ 15.3095, the values in Codenotti–Gerace–Resta 2003, Table 1.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ZeroErrorFrontier.WorldRecords.t2b_c27_world_record`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/WorldRecords.lean#L1833), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.WorldRecords.t2d_c31_world_record`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/WorldRecords.lean#L1875), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.CosetQuotient.t1f_baumert_pullback_homomorphism`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/CosetQuotient.lean#L1693); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Independent construction (Baumert expansion plus port systems); it does not formalise the 2003 sets and gives no new bound.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** These are not best known bounds: the 2003 table lists α(C₂₇^⊠4) ≥ 31522 and α(C₃₁^⊠4) ≥ 54934, above the repository's fourth-power bases 31466 and 54913 and above its final bounds.
- **Limit.** The 2003 entries are printed cardinalities marked as obtained by expansion formulas and experiment; the explicit sets were not examined in this audit.
- **Limit.** Θ is not defined in Lean; the expansion map is the known construction of Baumert et al. (1971).
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [zero-error-torus-frontier](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-016` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-016_zero-error-torus-frontier/Donahue_2026_zero_error_torus_frontier.pdf)

<a id="r40"></a>
### R40. Coset codes in the fourth strong power of C_n for n = 8k+1 with published cardinalities

- **Statement.** For every k ≥ 3 and n = 8k+1: α(C_n^⊠4) ≥ (4k² + ⌊k/2⌋)·n². The set is lifted from 4k² + ⌊k/2⌋ = ⌊n⌊n/8⌋/2⌋ points of ℤ_n², no two within circular distance 1 in coordinate one and 7 in coordinate two; no such point set is larger (n ≥ 8), and each one of size M lifts to M·n² points (n ≥ 15).
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ZeroErrorFrontier.CosetQuotient.t1e_infinite_hstar_family_and_ports`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/CosetQuotient.lean#L1206), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.CosetQuotient.t1a_coset_quotient_compression`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/CosetQuotient.lean#L249), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.CosetQuotient.t1b_exact_quotient_ceilings`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/CosetQuotient.lean#L533); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Same cardinalities as published bounds, obtained from cosets of ⟨(1,0,0,2),(0,1,0,4)⟩.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** For odd k the size equals n²(n²−n−8)/16, Theorem 1 (d = 3) of Codenotti, Gerace and Resta (2003); for even k it equals (n⁴−n³)/16, the Baumert et al. (1971) value.
- **Limit.** The repository does not cite the 2003 paper.
- **Limit.** The contract statement contains conflict-pattern facts for odd k but no port system; the n²-port system is a separate kernel-checked definition outside the audited 32 declarations.
- **Limit.** The companion theorem T1c is narrower than its prose: one of two claimed branches, n ≥ 9, ball sizes at four n.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [zero-error-torus-frontier](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-016` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-016_zero-error-torus-frontier/Donahue_2026_zero_error_torus_frontier.pdf)

<a id="r41"></a>
### R41. Haemers rank bound, Haemers's Schläfli-graph example and Lovász's pentagon bound

- **Statement.** If a matrix LR over a field, of inner width r, has nonzero diagonal and vanishes on all pairs of distinct non-adjacent vertices of G, then α(G^⊠d) ≤ r^d for all d. For the Schläfli graph S and its complement S̄: α(S^⊠d) ≤ 3^d, α(S̄^⊠d) ≤ 7^d and α(S ⊠ S̄) ≥ 27 > 21. For the pentagon: α(C₅^⊠2) ≥ 5 and α(C₅^⊠d)² ≤ 5^d.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ZeroErrorFrontier.HaemersParadox.t4a_haemers_rank_theorem`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/HaemersParadox.lean#L320), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.HaemersParadox.t4d_haemers_schlafli_paradox`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/HaemersParadox.lean#L1849), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.HaemersParadox.t4c_lovasz_pentagon_theorem`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/HaemersParadox.lean#L1404), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.HaemersParadox.t4b_integer_orthogonal_handle_sandwich`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/HaemersParadox.lean#L558); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Results of Haemers (1979) and Lovász (1979); integer forms, without real numbers.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** Θ and √5 are not defined in Lean; Θ(C₅) = √5 and Θ(S ⊠ S̄) > Θ(S)·Θ(S̄) are consequences outside Lean.
- **Limit.** That the defined 27-vertex graph is strongly regular (27,16,10,8) was checked by computation outside Lean; uniqueness of that graph is a cited fact.
- **Limit.** The orthogonal-representation bound T4b is proved for vectors of equal norm, while the paper states it for bounded norm.
- **Limit.** The claim to be the first such formal proof was not verified; the 1979 articles were not opened in this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [zero-error-torus-frontier](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-016` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-016_zero-error-torus-frontier/Donahue_2026_zero_error_torus_frontier.pdf)

<a id="r42"></a>
### R42. Two-factor combining rule for separation systems, table admissibility, and the seven-label graph

- **Statement.** If two label systems are realised by independent families in graphs G₁ and G₂, and a table assigns each target label a list of label pairs pairwise separated in at least one coordinate, then the unions of product blocks realise the target system in G₁ ⊠ G₂ with sizes Σ|R₁(a)|·|R₂(b)|. Five fixed tables pass the separation checks. For the seven-label graph G₇: α(G₇) ≥ 3 and α(G₇^⊠d) ≤ 3^d.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`ZeroErrorFrontier.SeparationCalculus.t3c_heterogeneous_composition_and_tables`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/SeparationCalculus.lean#L1071), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.SeparationCalculus.t3a_g7_induced_c5_and_exact_capacity`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/SeparationCalculus.lean#L260), [`ZeroErrorFrontier.SeparationCalculus.t3b_weighted_fractional_clique_barrier`](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier/blob/af343aaa1701637e23733ac0abd7a8f9b2e22b60/lean/ZeroErrorFrontier/SeparationCalculus.lean#L404); axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Two-input case of the BPZ combining rule (Tandon 2026, Proposition 1), allowing two alphabets.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement matches the stated claim; prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** This does not resolve the two-sided extension of Theorem 1 that Tandon (arXiv:2608.30273, Section 5 and Remark 3) leaves for future work: no Gao gadget, compatibility condition or profile formula is derived.
- **Limit.** The same rule exists for one alphabet in Tandon's Proposition 1 and in the Buys–Polak–Zuiddam Lean library (Realisation.multiSubst); the general theorem is never instantiated in the repository.
- **Limit.** The tables are those of Buys, Polak and Zuiddam; only their admissibility is re-checked.
- **Limit.** The G₇ bound is a 3-clique cover of the repository's own auxiliary graph; the weighted clique-cover theorem T3b gives upper bounds only (46875/2 is not shown optimal).
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [zero-error-torus-frontier](https://github.com/0thernes/zero-error-torus-frontier) `v1.0.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-016` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-016_zero-error-torus-frontier/Donahue_2026_zero_error_torus_frontier.pdf)

<a id="section-f"></a>
## F. Engineering invariant suites

*Machine-checked properties of a software model or simulator. They say the model is internally consistent, not that it describes nature.*

<a id="r43"></a>
### R43. Conservation and monotonicity facts for the repository's discrete vesicle, ATP and SNARE models

- **Statement.** For the repository's definitions: every valid vesicle-pool step list keeps rrp + recycling + reserve; the store (a₀ + s·t) ∸ (b + f·c)·t drops strictly when s < b + f·c and is 0 for all t ≥ ⌊a₀/D⌋ + 1, D = b + f·c − s; leak lowers the sustainable rate; (8n)/8 = n; the clamped SNARE barrier is non-increasing in Ca²⁺ and SNARE counts.
- **Evidence.** Lean kernel; declarations [`SynapseBouton.vesicle_pool_transition_invariant`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L297), [`SynapseBouton.vesicle_pool_multistep_invariant`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L306), [`SynapseBouton.atp_deficit_strict_depletion`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L319), [`SynapseBouton.atp_hitting_time_upper_bound`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L327), [`SynapseBouton.resting_leak_strictly_lowers_sustainable_rate`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L349), [`SynapseBouton.kinesin_processive_atp_exact`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L364), [`SynapseBouton.snare_barrier_monotone_in_syt1_ca`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L374), [`SynapseBouton.snare_copy_number_cooperativity`](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab/blob/06e0dcdd5fc4cb406e9fe21d260ff94b68a414d4/lean/Solution.lean#L393); axioms: propext, Quot.sound. True by construction of self-defined update rules; the H3 simulation outcome itself rests on Rust code outside Lean.
- **Audit (2026-11-26).** Rebuilt from a clean clone at the audited commit: pass; the formal statement is narrower than the usual informal claim (see Limits); prior work: known mathematics.
- **Limit.** T15 is an upper bound on the zero time, not an exact hitting time; it equals 3 s only for the deterministic mean-rate H3 constants, while the simulator jitters the rate each second.
- **Limit.** The ATP and SNARE constants are the author's and are not found in the cited sources; the Lean definitions are hand-written analogues of the TypeScript/Rust engines with no tested link.
- **Limit.** T17 contains no kinesin model; T18 and T19 are non-strict.
- **Limit.** No part of NEURO-001 (consciousness) or NEURO-019 (20 W credit assignment) is addressed.
- **Upstream.** The source repository has commits newer than the archived pin. They are not covered by this audit.
- **Check it.** `cd lean && lake build && lake env lean VerifyAxioms.lean`
- **Source.** [human-synapse-bouton-lab](https://github.com/0thernes/human-synapse-bouton-lab) `v1.3.0` · archive entry `0TH-2026-007` · [paper](papers/0TH-2026-007_human-synaptic-bouton-verification/Donahue_2026_human_synaptic_bouton_verification.pdf)

## Not claimed

- No Millennium Prize problem and no grand open problem is solved here. P versus NP is open.
- No result has been refereed by a journal or checked by a named outside expert.
- Engineering invariant suites (section F) verify software models. They are not evidence about consciousness, sentience, biology or physics.
- A search that found no earlier proof is not a proof of novelty.

## How a result gets on this list

1. The claim is registered in the archive with a pinned commit and a frozen paper.
2. The formal statement is read against the informal claim and against the cited source, in a session that did not write the proof.
3. The proof is rebuilt from a clean clone at that commit, or the ledger says it was not.
4. The literature is searched for earlier or parallel proofs and the outcome is recorded.
5. The wording is limited to what steps 2 to 4 support. Anything narrower than the usual informal claim is stated under Limit.

## How to challenge a result

- Open an issue on this repository or on the result's repository and quote the result number (for example R7).
- A reproducible counterexample, a gap in a statement audit, or an earlier proof in the literature leads to a correction: the result is narrowed, reclassified or withdrawn, and keeps its number.
- Corrections are recorded in CHANGELOG.md.

## What Would Prove Us Wrong (Falsification Protocol)

Any failing run of `python3 scripts/verify_archive.py`, `sha256sum -c CHECKSUMS.sha256`, or `python3 -m pytest -v tests/` immediately falsifies the corresponding integrity claim above. External critics can also independently clone any pinned submodule at its exact commit SHA and run the entry's `falsification_command` from `EVIDENCE.md`.

<!-- FILE: LIMITATIONS.md -->

# Limitations, Epistemic Boundaries & Real-vs-Metaphor (`LIMITATIONS.md`)

## 1. What This Master Archive Does and Does Not Guarantee

- **Cryptographic provenance, NOT external peer review:** `0thernes-research-archive` cryptographically locks frozen PDFs, exact Git submodule commits, Lean 4 axiom policies, and CI run links. None of the archived research preprints have undergone external journal peer review unless explicitly recorded with a publisher DOI.
- **No Mega-Atlas grand-problem retirement claimed:** As documented in [`builds/0TH-BUILD-007_unsolved-problems-mega-atlas/0THERNES_SOLVED_AUDIT_2026-11-25.md`](builds/0TH-BUILD-007_unsolved-problems-mega-atlas/0THERNES_SOLVED_AUDIT_2026-11-25.md), **0 of 1,900** grand open problems in `unsolved-problems-mega-atlas` are retired by entries in this archive; specialized theorems (such as Conjecture 7.7 of Banić & Elezović in `0TH-2026-006`) are proved within their exact cited scopes.
- **Historical snapshots vs. live repos:** Superseded repositories (`0TH-2026-001`, `002`, `003`, `005`) remain pinned as immutable historical snapshots for provenance while active unified research continues in `0TH-2026-009` (`pauli-contextuality-lab`). Historical `METADATA.json` records may retain earlier version metadata as frozen snapshots.
- **AI-assisted provenance:** Individual papers and builds were produced by solo researcher Alexander Stephen Donahue (`Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA`, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`) with disclosed AI assistance; epistemic trust rests on reproducible kernel verification and falsification commands in each entry's `EVIDENCE.md`.

## 2. Real vs. Metaphor

- **"Vault" / "Frozen":** Literally means committed Git blobs hashed with SHA-256 inside `CHECKSUMS.sha256` and verified on every push by GitHub Actions CI.
- **"Tier I / Tier II / Tier III":** Strict epistemic separation: Tier I holds standalone research preprints; Tier II holds engineering build white papers and embedded Pure Lean invariant suites; Tier III holds architectural laws, pre-registered empirical claims (including null results), finite computational certificates, and open-problem atlases—never conflated with Lean-proved general mathematical theorems.

<!-- FILE: REPLICATION.md -->

# Replication Protocol (`REPLICATION.md`)

Any third party can verify the entire canonical master archive, live ecosystem mirror, Mega-Atlas bridge, and DigiCert RFC 3161 TSA release seal from a clean clone:

```bash
# 1. Clone the archive (add --recursive to fetch every pinned public submodule).
#    Needs Python 3.10 or newer: the pinned test tools do not install on 3.9. CI uses 3.12.
git clone https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive.git
cd 0thernes-research-archive
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# 2. Verify every SHA-256 digest, RFC 3161 TSA seal, ORCID, axiom policy, bridge parity, table continuity,
#    zero broken links, every submodule pin, and the numbered Results Ledger (RESULTS.md)
python3 scripts/verify_archive.py
sha256sum -c CHECKSUMS.sha256
python3 scripts/build_ledger.py --check

# 3. Run automated integrity, privacy-firewall, failure-injection, property, negative, mutation & idempotence tests
python3 -m pytest -v tests/
python3 scripts/build_site.py
bash scripts/audit-repo.sh .
```

To refresh the live upstream status mirror against GitHub right now, run `python3 scripts/live_sync.py`. To verify a specific paper's Lean 4 formal proof from scratch, run `git submodule update --init repos/<slug>` and execute the exact `falsification_command` printed in `papers/<id>/EVIDENCE.md`.

# AGENTS.md — Canonical Agent Instructions (`0thernes-research-archive`)

This file is the canonical instruction file for all AI agents (`CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, and `.cursor/rules/build-standard.mdc` point here).

## Mission & Identity

- **Repository:** `https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive`
- **Author:** Alexander Stephen Donahue (`Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA`, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`, `0_0@0thernes.art`). Do NOT assert an unformed LLC entity in new headers or metadata.
- **Privacy Firewall (MANDATORY):** NEVER register, mention, or submodule private repositories or third-party forks. Every entry MUST be `PUBLIC`.

## Hard Rules (`R1`–`R8`)

1. Commit and push straight to `main` (`R1`/`R2`); CI is informational (`R3`); zero banned files such as `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` or `dependabot.yml` (`R4`).
2. Never fabricate SHA-256 digests, CI run URLs, DOIs, or peer-review status (`R6`).
3. Always run `python3 scripts/verify_archive.py --sync` after updating any PDF, artifact, or submodule pin, and copy `CHECKSUMS.sha256` to `data/MANIFEST.sha256`.
4. Classify every defect into one of the 10 Build Standard classes (`R7`; `docs/glossary.md`).

## Core Commands

```bash
just reproduce   # Verify archive, checksums, pytest suite, static site, and Build Standard audit
just sync        # Regenerate METADATA.json, EVIDENCE.md, registry/*.md, CHECKSUMS.sha256, data/MANIFEST.sha256
just test        # Run pytest integrity/property/negative/mutation suite
just audit       # Score repo against Build Standard v1.2.0
```

Two entries answer a question that another author stated as open in an arXiv preprint: Conjecture 7.7 of Banic and Elezovic (arXiv:2610.17046v1) in 0TH-2026-006, and the limit question of Section 6 of Muller and Saniga (arXiv:2609.19862v1) in 0TH-2026-009 Track 2, where the identification of the formal objects with the preprint's hypergraphs rests partly on argument outside Lean. 0TH-2026-009 Track 1 also proves Jonah's Conjecture E from an unreviewed Zenodo preprint, with Theorem B4 cited from outside Lean. ## How this mirror is refreshed

- **Scheduled pull (active):** [`.github/workflows/live-sync.yml`](../.github/workflows/live-sync.yml) queries the GitHub API every hour (`17 * * * *`), re-verifies SHA-256 integrity and `pytest`, and commits only when upstream state changed. GitHub may start scheduled runs late, so this table can lag the source repositories by an hour or more. The `Synced (UTC)` stamp above is the time of the last change, not of the last check.
- **Manual refresh (active):** run the workflow by hand (`workflow_dispatch`) or `python scripts/live_sync.py` locally.
- **Push dispatch (optional, needs setup):** an upstream repository with [`docs/upstream-notify-workflow.yml`](../docs/upstream-notify-workflow.yml) installed as `.github/workflows/notify-archive.yml` and an `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret triggers a refresh on every push to `main`. Without the secret the workflow skips the dispatch, and the hourly pull still applies.
- **Discovery inventory:** [`PUBLIC_REPO_INVENTORY.md`](PUBLIC_REPO_INVENTORY.md) lists every public, non-fork owner repository and marks unregistered repositories as candidates without promoting them into the epistemic archive.
- **Immutability rule:** Release-pinned frozen PDFs and Rekor-attested submodules are only advanced when matching frozen artifacts are archived; post-release upstream commits appear immediately as `AHEAD_OF_PIN` with live CI links.

<!-- FILE: docs/architecture.md -->

# Archive Architecture (`docs/architecture.md`)

`0thernes-research-archive` is the **single canonical public master hub** organizing all public scientific outputs authored by Alexander Stephen Donahue (`ORCID 0009-0006-8168-9648`) into **three strictly separated epistemic tiers** (**48 entries**: 19 Tier I + 17 Tier II + 12 Tier III), backed by **35 pinned public Git submodules** under `repos/`, a **26-row Solved Sub-Conjectures & Mega-Atlas V2 Bridge**, an **hourly-refreshed Upstream Ecosystem Mirror** (the current count is generated in `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json`), a unified SHA-256 integrity manifest (`CHECKSUMS.sha256` & `data/MANIFEST.sha256`), and an immutable DigiCert RFC 3161 TSA–sealed frozen release manifest (`data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256` + `data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256.tsr`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UP["Upstream Public 0thernes/* Repos (40 tracked)"] -->|repository_dispatch / 2h cron| LS["scripts/live_sync.py"]
    R1["registry/PAPERS.json<br/>Tier I: 18 Standalone Preprints"] --> V["scripts/verify_archive.py"]
    R2["registry/BUILD_PAPERS.json<br/>Tier II: 17 Builds · 1,058 Lean Decls"] --> V
    R3["registry/LAWS_AND_DISCOVERIES.json<br/>Tier III: 12 Laws, Claims & Atlases"] --> V
    BR["registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.json<br/>0/1900 Grand · 5 Peer Sub-Conjectures"] --> V
    LS --> LM["registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json/.md"]
    LM --> V
    S["repos/* (Pinned Public Submodules)"] --> V
    V --> C["CHECKSUMS.sha256 & data/MANIFEST.sha256"]
    V --> FZ["data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256 + DigiCert .tsr"]
    V --> D["Per-Entry METADATA.json + EVIDENCE.md"]
    V --> P["scripts/build_site.py -> WCAG 2.2 AA Pages Portal"]
```

## Verification Invariants

1. **Single-script deterministic derivation (`scripts/verify_archive.py --sync`):** Regenerates all `METADATA.json`, `EVIDENCE.md`, `registry/*.md`, `CHECKSUMS.sha256`, `data/MANIFEST.sha256`, and `data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256` directly from the canonical JSON registries (verified idempotent by B14 tests).
2. **Scheduled upstream mirror (`scripts/live_sync.py` + `.github/workflows/live-sync.yml`, hourly):** Tracks live `main` HEADs, latest releases, and CI status across every tracked public non-fork `0thernes/*` repository (count in `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json`) without disturbing immutable release-pinned frozen PDFs or invalidating `data/RELEASE_FREEZE.sha256.tsr`.
3. **Exact submodule commit pinning, table continuity & A24 size caps:** Every `pinned_commit` in `PAPERS.json` and `BUILD_PAPERS.json` matches `git ls-files --stage repos` (`34` submodules), `README.md` registry tables cannot be split by blank lines, `README.md` and `LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json` counts match exact registry totals, `SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.json` enforces exact version parity against the registries, and every archived file is strictly `< 5 MB`.
4. **Strict axiom, identity, link, TSA & ORCID enforcement:** Every entry carries ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`, zero unformed `"0thernes LLC"` assertions, an explicit `verification_boundary`, Lean axiom allowlists strictly within `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, valid DigiCert RFC 3161 TSA digest binding, and zero broken relative markdown links.
5. **Public-only privacy firewall:** Zero private repositories or third-party forks may appear anywhere in `registry/`, `repos/`, `llms.txt`, or `.gitmodules`.

<!-- FILE: docs/adr/0001-three-tier-epistemic-archive.md -->

# ADR 0001: Three-Tier Epistemic Separation and Pinned Submodule Vault Architecture

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-21 (formalized in ADR format 2026-11-25)

## Context
A single researcher producing both standalone machine-checked mathematical preprints, engineering systems with embedded formal invariant proofs, and empirical/exploratory open-problem atlases risks conflating distinct levels of proof rigor if all artifacts sit in one flat bibliography.

## Decision
Separate the public master archive into three machine-readable registries (`registry/PAPERS.json`, `registry/BUILD_PAPERS.json`, `registry/LAWS_AND_DISCOVERIES.json`), require an explicit `verification_boundary` on every entry, pin every public source repository as an exact Git submodule under `repos/`, and lock every frozen artifact with byte-exact SHA-256 digests (`CHECKSUMS.sha256` & `data/MANIFEST.sha256`) verified on every push.

## Consequences
- Readers and auditors can immediately distinguish 6-kernel Lean 4 proofs (Tier I) from engineering invariant suites (Tier II) and empirical/atlas registries (Tier III).
- Any upstream tampering or accidental submodule drift immediately fails `scripts/verify_archive.py`.


---

<!-- FILE: docs/adr/0002-canonical-hub-and-live-sync.md -->

# ADR 0002: Single Canonical Public Hub, Atlas Consolidation, and Real-Time Live Sync

- **Status:** Accepted (`2026-11-25`)
- **Author:** Alexander Stephen Donahue (Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA; ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`)
- **Supersedes:** Scattered ad-hoc manual synchronization across specialist catalogues

## Context

Across the `0thernes` GitHub ecosystem, five repositories previously appeared to act as overlapping "lists or archives":

1. `0thernes/0thernes-research-archive` — Public cryptographic master vault of all Tier I preprints, Tier II build white papers & Lean 4 suites, and Tier III laws/discoveries/atlases.
2. `0thernes/unsolved-problems-mega-atlas` — Cross-disciplinary 1,900-problem open-problems connectome (`0TH-BUILD-007`).
3. `0thernes/unsolved-mathematics` — Mathematics-focused open-problem atlas and 8-domain Lean 4 structural core (`0TH-BUILD-004`, `0TH-DISC-005`).
4. `0thernes/unsolved-black-hole-problems` — 16-problem ranked black-hole physics catalogue (`0TH-DISC-006`).
5. Private research staging repositories (strictly non-public; never referenced or indexed in public vaults).

Without a unified live-sync layer and cross-atlas bridge, readers and agents had to inspect multiple repositories to answer basic questions: *"Which repository is the authoritative master list?"*, *"Which upstream repos have moved ahead of their frozen release pin?"*, and *"Have any of the 1,900 Mega-Atlas problems or smaller peer-literature conjectures been formally proved?"*

## Decision

1. **Single Canonical Public Hub:** Establish `0thernes/0thernes-research-archive` (and its GitHub Pages portal `https://0thernes.github.io/0thernes-research-archive/`) as the **one authoritative public master hub**. Specialist open-problem catalogues remain focused domain spokes indexed inside Tier II / Tier III and link back to the hub.
2. **Authoritative Solved-Subconjecture & Mega-Atlas Bridge:** Maintain `registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.json` (and derived `.md`) inside this hub, explicitly enforcing `grand_problems_retired = 0 / 1900` while indexing every machine-checked peer-literature sub-conjecture, bounded partial result, barrier formalization, and discrete invariant suite.
3. **Hybrid Pull + Push Real-Time Live Sync (Preserving Release Immutability):**
   - **Pull-based scheduled mirror (zero secrets required):** `.github/workflows/live-sync.yml` runs `scripts/live_sync.py` every 2 hours (`0 */2 * * *`) using the standard `GITHUB_TOKEN` to refresh `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json/.md`, update `README.md`'s bounded live status block, re-run `verify_archive.py --sync` + `pytest`, and commit straight to `main` (which immediately redeploys GitHub Pages).
   - **Push-based instant dispatch (opt-in):** Upstream repos carrying `.github/workflows/notify-archive.yml` (template in `docs/upstream-notify-workflow.yml`) fire `repository_dispatch` (`upstream-repo-updated`) on every `main` push once `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` is configured.
   - **Why we do NOT inject commits into already-attested Tier I release repos:** Pushing cosmetic workflow files onto completed, Sigstore/Rekor-attested releases would break `HEAD == release_tag` parity and trigger redundant 20-minute 6-kernel CI runs. The 2-hour scheduled pull mirror already tracks every public repo automatically without disturbing immutable release tags.
4. **Strict Public-Only Privacy Firewall:** `scripts/live_sync.py` rejects any repository where `private == true`, `fork == true`, or `owner != 0thernes`, enforced both at runtime and in `tests/test_archive_integrity.py`.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** One single canonical source of truth, automatically refreshed live mirror and GitHub Pages portal, zero broken cross-atlas links, and strict separation between immutable frozen release pins and live upstream `main` HEADs.
- **Trade-off:** Instant sub-minute push updates require setting one optional `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret on upstream repos; without it, sync latency is bounded by the 2-hour schedule (or instant via manual `workflow_dispatch`).

## Update (2026-11-26): what is actually running

An audit of the workflow history and the upstream repositories on 2026-11-26 found that the push path had never fired: 0 of the hub's sync runs were started by `repository_dispatch`, 2 of the 41 tracked repositories carried a notify workflow, and none had the `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret. The mirror is therefore a scheduled pull, and calling it "real-time" overstated it. Changes made:

- The schedule moved from every 2 hours to hourly (`17 * * * *`; minute 17 avoids the top-of-hour queue, where GitHub delays scheduled runs most).
- Generated and hand-written text now says "refreshed hourly" and states that push dispatch is optional and not configured.
- The mirror's `synced_utc` stamp is the time of the last change in upstream state, not of the last check; the generated page says so.

Push-triggered refresh remains available as an owner action: create one fine-grained token that may send `repository_dispatch` to this repository, and store it as `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` in each upstream repository that carries the notify workflow. Tokens are never created or stored by automation in this repository. The numbered results list ([ADR 0003](0003-numbered-results-ledger.md)) does not depend on this path: it joins versions and pins from the registries on every sync and marks results whose source has moved past the audited commit.


---

<!-- FILE: docs/adr/0003-numbered-results-ledger.md -->

# ADR 0003: One Numbered Results Ledger

- **Status:** Accepted (`2026-11-26`)
- **Author:** Alexander Stephen Donahue (Independent Researcher, Spokane, WA, USA; ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`)
- **Builds on:** [ADR 0002](0002-canonical-hub-and-live-sync.md) (single canonical hub and live sync)

## Context

The hub answers "which repositories exist and are they intact". It did not answer, in one readable place, "what exactly has been proven". That information was spread across long table cells in `README.md`, the Mega-Atlas bridge and each paper, written per repository rather than per result, and mixed with build and provenance detail. A reader could not see a plain list of results, and a claim's wording was never tied to an audit of the statement itself.

## Decision

1. **One list.** `RESULTS.md` is the single numbered list of results. It is generated; nobody edits it by hand.
2. **One source.** `registry/RESULTS_LEDGER.json` holds one record per audited result: a plain statement, its kind, its evidence, the question it answers (if any), the Lean declarations with file and line, the commit that was audited, the audit outcome, its limits and a check command.
3. **Joined, not copied.** Version, repository, pin and paper path are not stored in the ledger. `scripts/build_ledger.py` joins them from `registry/PAPERS.json` and `registry/BUILD_PAPERS.json`, and reads the live mirror for upstream state. The ledger therefore follows every registry update and every live sync without anyone retyping a number.
4. **An audit is tied to a commit.** Evidence links are permalinks at the audited commit. If the archive pin moves past it, the result is shown as "re-audit pending". If the source repository moves past the pin, the result says so.
5. **Nothing is silently missing.** Every Tier I and Tier II entry appears: through its results, through a stated reason, or under "registered but not yet audited into this ledger".
6. **Numbers are permanent.** A result that is narrowed keeps its number. A result that fails is marked withdrawn and keeps its number.
7. **Wording is checked.** The generator rejects promotional wording, a "published open question answered" without a cited source and a recorded statement audit and prior-work search, a "new theorem" that is known mathematics, and a kernel-checked result without a cited declaration.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** one page a reader can check line by line; counts in `README.md` come from the ledger; the list cannot drift from the registries; a release or a pin move cannot inherit an audit it did not have.
- **Cost:** a result enters the list only after a statement audit, so the ledger can lag behind a new paper. The lag is visible, by design.
- **Limit:** the audit is an internal, AI-assisted check directed by the author. It is not peer review, and the ledger says so at the top.

## How to use

```bash
python scripts/build_ledger.py            # regenerate RESULTS.md and the README block
python scripts/build_ledger.py --check    # fail if the ledger is invalid or the outputs are stale
python scripts/build_ledger.py --check --checkouts <dir>   # also confirm each Lean declaration is at the cited line
```

`python scripts/verify_archive.py --sync` runs the first form; `python scripts/verify_archive.py` runs the second.


---

<!-- FILE: docs/faq.md -->

# Frequently Asked Questions (`docs/faq.md`)

### 1. Which repository is the single canonical master archive of everything `0thernes` has solved or verified?
**This repository (`0thernes/0thernes-research-archive`)** — along with its live GitHub Pages portal at [`https://0thernes.github.io/0thernes-research-archive/`](https://0thernes.github.io/0thernes-research-archive/). Specialist open-problem catalogues (`unsolved-problems-mega-atlas`, `unsolved-mathematics`, `unsolved-black-hole-problems`) remain focused domain spokes indexed inside this hub and refreshed hourly via [`.github/workflows/live-sync.yml`](../.github/workflows/live-sync.yml) (see [ADR 0002](adr/0002-canonical-hub-and-live-sync.md)).

### 2. Why are entries split into Tier I, Tier II, and Tier III?
To enforce epistemic honesty: Tier I holds standalone formalized research preprints (`PAPERS.json`), Tier II holds public software/engineering builds with embedded white papers and Pure Lean 4 invariant suites (`BUILD_PAPERS.json`), and Tier III holds architectural laws, pre-registered empirical claims (including null results), finite certificates, synthesis dossiers, and open-problem atlases (`LAWS_AND_DISCOVERIES.json`).

### 3. Have any papers in this archive retired one of the 1,900 Mega-Atlas problems?
**No (`0 / 1,900` grand Mega-Atlas problems retired).** Four peer-literature open sub-conjectures/questions (`0TH-2026-006` Conjecture 7.7, `0TH-2026-010` Vinciguerra Sec. 6, `0TH-2026-009` Track 2 Muller–Saniga Sec. 6, `0TH-2026-012` (coded-PIR identities, not a resolved question)) plus Jonah's Conjecture E (`0TH-2026-009` Track 1, with cited Theorem B4 outside Lean) are formally proved in Lean 4.35.0 within their exact published scopes; see [`registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.md`](../registry/SOLVED_AND_ATLAS_BRIDGE.md) and [`builds/0TH-BUILD-007_unsolved-problems-mega-atlas/0THERNES_SOLVED_AUDIT_2026-11-25.md`](../builds/0TH-BUILD-007_unsolved-problems-mega-atlas/0THERNES_SOLVED_AUDIT_2026-11-25.md).

### 4. How does the hub stay in step with the upstream repositories?
Every hour (and immediately when an upstream repository that carries `.github/workflows/notify-archive.yml` and an `ARCHIVE_SYNC_TOKEN` secret dispatches `upstream-repo-updated`; no repository had that secret on 2026-11-26), `.github/workflows/live-sync.yml` runs `scripts/live_sync.py`, updates `registry/LIVE_ECOSYSTEM_MIRROR.json/.md` and the bounded live status block in `README.md`, re-verifies SHA-256 digests and `pytest`, and redeploys GitHub Pages automatically.

### 5. How do I verify every archived PDF, link, and submodule pin locally?
Run `python3 scripts/verify_archive.py`, `sha256sum -c CHECKSUMS.sha256`, and `python3 -m pytest -v tests/`. Every hash, relative link, privacy-firewall invariant, and Git submodule pin is verified in seconds.
